answer: An honest AI node must expend 1 unit of compute to generate a verified output task, whereas 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 units, making this a strictly non-amortizable process. A verifier uses an atlas of past state transitions to track work, rejecting any duplicate output signature. If the verifier detects a delta between expected work and output nectar, the identity is banned without refund. This ensures verified-work stability.
